name: Gade
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Weise 2013 subclassification discussion on Glottolog; no phonological description of Gade (Nigeria) located.

sources.citation: Sterk, Jan P. 1990. Features of vowel assimilation in Gade (a language in evolution). Journal of West African Languages 20(1): 118-124.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Silent on stress and on tone; the article treats only vowel assimilation (nine-vowel ATR system, V+V across verb-object boundary). Footnote 1 gives the fieldwork locale (Kuje, FCT, 1976-77) and autonym Babyé/Ribyé.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2013. The Nupoid languages of west-central Nigeria: overview and comparative wordlist. Working document, 14 March 2013. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 Tone (p. 8): all Nupoid languages incl. Gade have three level tones plus two glide tones (analysable as three underlying levels); 'Nupe, Gbari and Gade seem to exhibit downdrift, but do not have terraced tones.' No statement about stress. Gade data are second-hand from Sterk 1978a (= the 1977 dissertation).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1989. Nupoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo languages, 305-322. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 14.3.3 Tone (pp. 314-315): Gade has three level tones, two glides and a surface lowered mid-tone; quotes Sterk (1978:8) that 'the few lexical items that have underlying glide tones should probably be analyzed as cases where word-internal vowel clusters contracted'; downdrift, no terracing. No stress statement.
